defs.def:experiment-pair-class: \(\mathcal Q_{\mathrm{spec},n}=\{(P,\bar g_n):\text{ for this }n,\ (P,\bar g_n)\text{ satisfies }\text{ass:pair-law-membership}\text{ and }\text{ass:admissible-external-code}\}\).

assumptions.ass:treatment-subgaussian:
With the exact Luxemburg convention
\[
 \lVert W\rVert_{\psi_2}
 =\inf\{u>0:E_P[\exp(W^2/u^2)]\le2\},
\]
the treatment noise satisfies \(\lVert\eta\rVert_{\psi_2}\le\psi_{\eta}\).

snapshot.stmt: There exists \(c>0\), depending only on the displayed class constants and \(\alpha\), such that every \(\mathcal A\in\mathfrak H_\alpha\) satisfies \(\liminf_{n\to\infty}r_n^{-1}\sup_{(P,\bar g_n)\in\mathcal Q_{\mathrm{spec},n}}W_n(\mathcal A,P,\bar g_n)\ge c\). Therefore the bias-aware spectral band has minimax expected sup-width order \(r_n=(\log n/n)^{\beta/(2\beta+1)}\) over the same fixed positive code-error pair class. The lower bound ranges over every measurable band, not only contour-based, symmetric, or fixed-width bands.

defs.def:honest-band-class: \(\mathfrak H_\alpha=\{\mathcal A=(\mathcal A_n)_{n\ge1}:\mathcal A\text{ is measurable in the sample and fixed external code and satisfies }\text{ass:asymptotic-band-honesty}\}\).

assumptions.ass:asymptotic-band-honesty: \(\liminf_{n\to\infty}\inf_{(P,\bar g_n)\in\mathcal Q_{\mathrm{spec},n}}P\{\tau_0(v)\in\mathcal A_n(v;\bar g_n)\text{ for every }v\in\mathcal I\}\ge1-\alpha\).

snapshot.stmt:
For fixed \(P\), \(g\in\mathcal G\), and bounded \(g'\), the infimum over \(d\in\mathcal D_{\gamma_D,L_D}\) in \(d_P(g,g')\) is attained. If
\[
 d_P^{\mathrm{dir}}(g,g')=\operatorname*{ess\,sup}_{v\in[0,1]}
 E_P[|g'(X,V)-g(X,V)|\mid V=v],
\]
\[
 \Gamma_{\mathrm{dir}}(P,\varepsilon_0)
 =\{g\in\mathcal G:d_P^{\mathrm{dir}}(g,g_0)\le\varepsilon_0\},
 \qquad
 a_{\mathcal G}^{\mathrm{dir}}(P)=\inf_{g\in\mathcal G}d_P^{\mathrm{dir}}(g,g_0),
\]
then \(\Gamma_{\mathrm{dir}}(P,\varepsilon_0)\subseteq\Gamma(P,\varepsilon_0)\) and \(a_{\mathcal G}(P)\le a_{\mathcal G}^{\mathrm{dir}}(P)\). If \(a_{\mathcal G}(P)\le\varepsilon_{\mathrm{app}}<\varepsilon_0\), then \(\Gamma(P,\varepsilon_0)\ne\varnothing\). Moreover, if \(g_0=0\), \(\varepsilon_0<a\le C_g\), and \(\mathcal G\) contains the constant code \(g_a(x,v)=-a\), then \(g_a\in\Gamma(P,\varepsilon_0)\setminus\Gamma_{\mathrm{dir}}(P,\varepsilon_0)\).

defs.def:external-input-ball:
Let
\[
 \mathcal D_{\gamma_D,L_D}
 =\left\{d:[0,1]\to[-2C_g,2C_g]:
 \sup_{u\ne v}\frac{|d(u)-d(v)|}{|u-v|^{\gamma_D}}\le L_D\right\}.
\]
Define
\[
 \Gamma(P,\varepsilon_0)
 =\left\{g\in\mathcal G:
 \inf_{d\in\mathcal D_{\gamma_D,L_D}}
 \operatorname*{ess\,sup}_{v\in[0,1]}
 E_P[|g_0(X,V)-g(X,V)-d(V)|\mid V=v]
 \le\varepsilon_0\right\},
\]
where \(\varepsilon_0\in(\varepsilon_{\mathrm{app}},\varepsilon_\star]\) is fixed after \(\mathfrak C_0\) and its maximal radius are derived and before the inference sample.
